title: Animate an image
description: Turn a finished image into the opening frame of a moving scene.

sections.title: Choose the first frame
steps: Select Wan 2.2 or LTX-2.5. Choose LTX “with sound” if you want generated audio.
Click First frame beside the prompt and choose an image from the library or Choose File…. You can also drop a local image into the box.
Check the image’s shape against Size and begin with a short Length, such as about 2 seconds.
Alternatively, right-click a picture in Library and choose Animate. This prepares a video request; check the selected model and settings before generating.

sections.title: Describe the movement that follows
paragraphs: The image supplies the starting appearance. Concentrate on what should move and how the camera should behave. Wan’s official image-to-video prompting guidance emphasizes action instead of repeating static details already in the picture.
sections.prompt: The leaves sway gently in a light breeze. A few ripples move across the water. The camera stays in the same position, and the main subject remains in view.

sections.title: Keep the starting frame close
paragraphs: LTX shows Strength with a first-frame image. Begin at its default of 0, which holds the conditioning frame. Raising it allows more departure from that frame; it is not a motion-speed control. Wan holds the first frame without offering a Strength slider.

The source can be resized or cropped to fit the output dimensions. Even with a held starting frame, later frames can change appearance. Keep the requested motion simple if preserving the subject is important.

sections.title: Generate and save
steps: Click Generate and wait for the completed clip.
Play it through. If the subject changes too much, reduce the complexity of the movement, use a shorter clip, or try a new seed.
Use Export… on the video to save the MP4. Keep its poster PNG as well if you are moving the original library files and want the generation details.

sections.title: Continue a finished clip
steps: Select a finished Zephra video and choose Extend Clip from its available actions.
Wait for the Continues from thumbnail to appear. Zephra prepares the end of that clip as the starting context.
Keep the original model and dimensions for continuity. Update the prompt to describe what happens next, and choose the length of the next part.
Click Generate. Zephra joins the continuation to the source and saves a new result; the original clip remains.
sections.note: Animate from Last Frame starts a separate video from the end of a clip. Extend Clip joins the new part onto the existing one. Clearing or replacing the reference leaves continuation mode.
